data.narrative:
Defense Unicorns, a Series B defense and security technology company, has raised $171M to date against a last post-money valuation of $1.0B. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of ten peers—two public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and eight private—all operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using a standard 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier applied to the $1.0B base, implies a valuation of $1.9B. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same-stage comparables—Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Heven AeroTech ($1.0B)—yields a median of $1.1B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in revenue, growth profile, and defensibility within the defense-tech cohort.

Triangulation of these methods produces a valuation range of $956M to $2.2B, with a median of $1.5B. The current $1.0B post-money valuation sits at the lower bound, supported by peer-median logic but below the stage-progression implication. Key uncertainties include revenue visibility, customer concentration risk among U.S. defense buyers, and regulatory pathway clarity. A $1.2B–$1.6B range appears most defensible given peer positioning and stage norms.
